**Irish ports with 10 000–100 000 passenger visits in both 2022 and 2023**

| Port | 2022 passenger visits | 2023 passenger visits |
|------|-----------------------|-----------------------|
| **Killybegs** | 11,146 | 27,910 |

In the RoPax sector, the third quarter is consistently the busiest period for ferry passengers and passenger vehicles. In 2020 and 2021, no other Irish shipping sector was impacted more by COVID-19 restrictions than this one. By 2023, passenger numbers had largely returned to normal, though they still remain below pre-COVID levels.

# Passenger Market
In the ROI passenger market, Q3 passenger numbers averaged 1.1 million in the three summers before the onset of COVID-19, i.e. Q3 2017 – Q3 2019. In the post-COVID period, i.e. Q3 2022 – Q3 2024, average third quarter numbers have fallen by 11% to approximately 1 million. Similarly, the number of passenger vehicles in the post-COVID era is 4% below that of pre-COVID.

# Ireland to receive 230,000 cruise passengers in 2023 at Dun Laoghaire
DUBLIN, Ireland: Ireland's second busiest cruise port, Dun Laoghaire, is expecting 90 cruise ships to unload passengers visiting Ireland this year.
This would set a record for Dun Laoghaire. In 2022, 65 cruise ships docked at Dun Laoghaire.
Ireland's busiest cruise port is Cork/Cobh.
Among those tourists entering Ireland at Dun Laoghaire will include 164,000 passengers and 71,000 crew members, according to tourism officials.
Further, 44 percent of those visitors will explore Dun Laoghaire Town and the surrounding area.
Beyond spending in local businesses, revenues from cruise passengers is being used to restore the historic harbor in Dun Laoghaire.
"The benefits of these cruises extend further, with job creation in various roles, such as tourist cabin, security staff, and tender escort boats," noted Dun Laoghaire town councillor Mary Hanafin, as quoted by Breakingnews.ie.
Frank Curran, Chief Executive, Dun Laoghaire County Council, noted the "significant income" brought to the community by cruise ship passengers contributes to the restoration of the 200-year-old harbor and to future plans, which include a national Water Sports Campus, according to Breakingnews.ie.
Among the cruise lines docking in Dun Laoghaire in 2023, Norwegian Cruise Lines will bring the most ships with 20, followed by Viking Cruise Lines with 17 dockings.
In 2022, ships docking in Dun Laoghaire saw 79,000 passengers and 44,000 crew visiting the area.

Among those tourists entering Ireland at Dun Laoghaire will include 164,000 passengers and 71,000 crew members, according to tourism officials.
Further, 44 percent of those visitors will explore Dun Laoghaire Town and the surrounding area.
Beyond spending in local businesses, revenues from cruise passengers is being used to restore the historic harbor in Dun Laoghaire.
"The benefits of these cruises extend further, with job creation in various roles, such as tourist cabin, security staff, and tender escort boats," noted Dun Laoghaire town councillor Mary Hanafin, as quoted by Breakingnews.ie.

Among the cruise lines docking in Dun Laoghaire in 2023, Norwegian Cruise Lines will bring the most ships with 20, followed by Viking Cruise Lines with 17 dockings.

# Statistics of Port Traffic Q4 and Year 2023
## Irish ports handled 47.8 million tonnes of goods in 2023
### Key Findings
*   Total tonnes of goods handled by Irish ports was 47.8 million tonnes in 2023, down by 10% compared with 2022.

*   Goods forwarded from Irish ports amounted to 15.7 million tonnes in 2023, while a total of 32.1 million tonnes of goods were received.

*   During 2023, 12,191 vessels arrived in Irish ports, compared with 12,517 in 2022.

*   Dublin port accounted for 58% of all vessel arrivals in Irish ports in 2023.

# Statistics of Port Traffic Q4 and Year 2023
## Irish ports handled 47.8 million tonnes of goods in 2023
### Statistician's Comment
The Central Statistics Office (CSO) has today (28 May 2024) published Statistics of Port Traffic results for 2023.
Commenting on the annual figures, Damien Lenihan, Statistician in the Transport Division, said: “_Irish ports handled 47.8 million tonnes of goods in 2023. This is a decrease of 10% compared with 2022. Goods forwarded from Irish ports amounted to 15.7 million tonnes in 2023, while a total of 32.1 million tonnes of goods were received._
_Great Britain & Northern Ireland accounted for 36% of the total tonnage of goods handled in the main ports by region of trade in 2023, while EU countries accounted for 44% of the total tonnage of goods handled in the main ports._

# Statistics of Port Traffic Q4 and Year 2023
## Irish ports handled 47.8 million tonnes of goods in 2023
### Key Findings
*   Total tonnes of goods handled by Irish ports was 47.8 million tonnes in 2023, down by 10% compared with 2022.

*   Goods forwarded from Irish ports amounted to 15.7 million tonnes in 2023, while a total of 32.1 million tonnes of goods were received.

*   During 2023, 12,191 vessels arrived in Irish ports, compared with 12,517 in 2022.

*   Dublin port accounted for 58% of all vessel arrivals in Irish ports in 2023.

# Statistics of Port Traffic Q4 and Year 2023
## Irish ports handled 47.8 million tonnes of goods in 2023
### Statistician's Comment
The Central Statistics Office (CSO) has today (28 May 2024) published Statistics of Port Traffic results for 2023.
Commenting on the annual figures, Damien Lenihan, Statistician in the Transport Division, said: “_Irish ports handled 47.8 million tonnes of goods in 2023. This is a decrease of 10% compared with 2022. Goods forwarded from Irish ports amounted to 15.7 million tonnes in 2023, while a total of 32.1 million tonnes of goods were received._
_Great Britain & Northern Ireland accounted for 36% of the total tonnage of goods handled in the main ports by region of trade in 2023, while EU countries accounted for 44% of the total tonnage of goods handled in the main ports._

# Statistics of Port Traffic Q4 and Year 2023
## Irish ports handled 47.8 million tonnes of goods in 2023
### Statistician's Comment

## Irish ports handled 47.8 million tonnes of goods in 2023
### Statistician's Comment
#### Cruise ships
_A total of 272 cruise ships arrived in Irish ports in 2023 compared with 240 in 2022. That was 43 less compared with pre-COVID-19 figures_ _, when 315 cruise ships visited Ireland in 2019. # Statistics of Port Traffic Q4 and Year 2023
## Irish ports handled 47.8 million tonnes of goods in 2023
### Key Findings
*   Total tonnes of goods handled by Irish ports was 47.8 million tonnes in 2023, down by 10% compared with 2022.

*   Goods forwarded from Irish ports amounted to 15.7 million tonnes in 2023, while a total of 32.1 million tonnes of goods were received.

*   During 2023, 12,191 vessels arrived in Irish ports, compared with 12,517 in 2022.

*   Dublin port accounted for 58% of all vessel arrivals in Irish ports in 2023.
